findings.title: Detach background writes from request cancellation
findings.body: All four background writes derive their timeout context from the incoming request context. HTTP request contexts are canceled when the handler returns, so returning after launching the goroutine cancels the legacy write rather than giving it ten seconds to finish. This makes successful unified writes routinely fail to reach the legacy safety copy. Preserve context values but detach cancellation before applying the background timeout.

findings.title: Mirror the committed update instead of reapplying UpdatedObjectInfo
findings.body: The legacy update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of a wrapper containing the object committed to unified storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute a patch against the supplied old object; evaluating it again against a stale legacy object can produce different contents or fail (for example, a JSON Patch test can succeed in unified storage and fail in legacy). Restore mirroring of the committed result so both stores receive the same update.

findings.title: Preserve write ordering for each resource
findings.body: Each successful mutation launches an independent goroutine with no ordering relative to other mutations of the same resource. A client can create an object and then delete it after receiving the create response, yet the legacy delete can execute before the legacy create, leaving a deleted object resurrected in the safety copy. Updates can likewise overwrite newer values with older ones. Background replication needs per-resource ordering or equivalent version-aware reconciliation.

findings.title: Do not use object names as metric kind labels
findings.body: The successful delete duration is recorded with name in the argument used elsewhere for options.Kind. This creates a separate metric label value for every deleted resource, causing unbounded Prometheus series cardinality, and prevents successful and failed delete measurements from being aggregated under the same kind. Pass the kind rather than the resource name.

findings.title: Record durations against the store actually called
findings.body: The background legacy DeleteCollection call records its outcome as a storage duration, so unified storage gets two samples per successful collection deletion and is blamed for legacy failures, while legacy gets no samples. Similarly, the unified Create and Update error paths at lines 45 and 129 record legacy durations despite never calling legacy. These misclassifications make store-specific error rates and latency metrics incorrect; use the appropriate store recorder in each path.
